tickerText: [TENNIS] Team Europe reclaimed the Laver Cup with a 13-5 win over Team World on Sept. 27 at London's O2 as Alexander Zverev closed it out 7-6(3), 6-3 over Learner Tien after Flavio Cobolli and Jakub Mensik beat Alex de Minaur and Taylor Fritz 7-5, 6-3 — Zverev's fourth Laver Cup clincher • [SQUASH] Malaysia swept Asian Games singles gold on Sept. 27 in Nagoya as Sivasangari Subramaniam beat Anahat Singh 11-4, 11-4, 11-7 and Ng Eain Yow downed Abhay Singh 11-9, 11-5, 11-5, with both winners earning LA28 Olympic quotas • [BADMINTON] Singapore's Loh Kean Yew stunned world No. 1 Jonatan Christie 21-14, 21-19 in the men's singles quarters on Sept. 27 at Ichinomiya, guaranteeing Singapore's first Asian Games men's singles medal as semis run Sept. 28 • [PICKLEBALL] The 1,000-point Rate Las Vegas Open opens Sept. 28 at the Darling Tennis Center with amateur brackets from 8 a.m. and pro qualifying Monday as Anna Leigh Waters chases career title No. 200 in doubles • [TABLE TENNIS] China swept Sept. 27 gold at Sky Hall Toyota as Wang Manyu beat Sun Yingsha 4-2 in the women's singles final and Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng edged Japan's Harimoto and Shinozuka 4-2 in men's doubles

newsItems.title: Europe Wins Laver Cup
newsItems.excerpt: Alexander Zverev sealed Team Europe's 13-5 victory over Team World on Sept. 27 at the O2, beating Learner Tien 7-6(3), 6-3 after Cobolli and Mensik won doubles to claim Europe's sixth Laver Cup title.

newsItems.title: Malaysia Sweeps Squash Gold
newsItems.excerpt: Sivasangari Subramaniam and Ng Eain Yow defended their Asian Games singles titles on Sept. 27 in Nagoya, beating India's Anahat Singh and Abhay Singh in straight games to claim LA28 Olympic quotas.

newsItems.title: Vegas Open Week Begins
newsItems.excerpt: The Carvana PPA Tour's Rate Las Vegas Open starts Sept. 28 at the Darling Tennis Center with amateur play and more than $1 million on offer, as Anna Leigh Waters eyes career title No. 200 in doubles.

newsItems.title: China Doubles Up at Asiad
newsItems.excerpt: Wang Manyu beat Sun Yingsha 4-2 in the women's singles final on Sept. 27, and Lin Shidong and Huang Youzheng took men's doubles gold 4-2 over Japan as China closed a strong day at Sky Hall Toyota.
